title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Interpretive Note on the Steady-Earner Wage Cap Fraction
content:
The credit of a dependency redetermination on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record is held within a wage cap: a base-period-wage fraction times the base-period wages on the claim. This note sets out which fraction that cap uses.

## The rule

The base-period-wage fraction for a dependency redetermination is:

- **0.36** (the steady-earner standard fraction) when the standard base period was used, base-period wages are at least 3.0 times high-quarter wages, and the entitlement credited on the claim already reaches the program's base-period-wage fraction times base-period wages, rounded down to the whole dollar;
- **0.35** (the steady-earner alternate fraction) when the alternate base period was used, base-period wages are at least 3.0 times high-quarter wages, and the entitlement credited on the claim already reaches that wage-capped amount;
- the program's base-period-wage fraction for any other dependency redetermination.

## Terms

- **Base period used, base-period wages and high-quarter wages** are those on the claim from its latest monetary determination.
- **Entitlement credited on the claim** is the total of every entitlement-credit entry in the claim's payment history.
- **The wage-capped amount** is the program's base-period-wage fraction times base-period wages, rounded down to the whole dollar.

## Conditions in combination

| Base period used | Base-period wages at least 3.0 times high-quarter wages | Entitlement credited reaches the wage-capped amount | Fraction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | Yes | Yes | 0.36 |
| Alternate | Yes | Yes | 0.35 |
| Standard or alternate | No | Either | The program's fraction |
| Standard or alternate | Either | No | The program's fraction |

### Hypothetical reading

A Regular State Unemployment Insurance claim on the standard base period with high-quarter wages of 9000.00 and base-period wages of 30000.00 (more than 3.0 times 9000.00, that is 27000.00), whose credited entitlement totals 9999.00 against a wage-capped amount of 0.3333 times 30000.00 rounded down, that is 9999, uses 0.36: its wage cap is 0.36 times 30000.00, that is 10800.00. Had its credited entitlement totalled 9000.00, the program's fraction would apply.
